title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Consolidated Results of Operations overview and revenue drivers
key_points: FY2022 total revenues of $66,608 million increased $4,322 million versus 2021, driven by higher BCA and BGS revenues partially offset by lower BDS revenues.

BCA revenues increased $6,374 million in 2022 primarily on higher 737 and 787 deliveries; BGS increased $1,283 million on higher commercial services volume; BDS decreased $3,378 million on development program charges, unfavorable performance across other defense programs, and lower P-8 and weapons volume.
raw_excerpt: Revenues increased by $4,322 million in 2022 compared with 2021 driven by higher revenues at BCA and BGS, partially offset by lower revenues at BDS. BCA revenues increased by $6,374 million primarily driven by higher 737 and 787 deliveries.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — FY23 appropriations funding Boeing's major DoD/NASA programs; 28% of BDS backlog non-U.S. (p.35)
key_points: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (enacted December 2022) provided $817 billion for the U.S. DoD and $25.4 billion for NASA.
FY23 appropriations included funding for Boeing's major programs: F/A-18 Super Hornet, F-15EX, CH-47 Chinook, AH-64 Apache, V-22 Osprey, KC-46A Tanker, MQ-25, and the Space Launch System.
FY23 appropriations did not include funding for additional P-8 aircraft; the P-8 program continues to pursue additional sales opportunities to extend production beyond 2024.
FY23 appropriations support F/A-18 production further into calendar year 2025.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — Named U.S. military service customers: USAF KC-46A, U.S. Navy MQ-25, T-7A Red Hawk (p.87)
key_points: KC-46A Tanker: in 2011 Boeing was awarded a contract from the USAF to design, develop, manufacture and deliver four next-generation aerial refueling tankers plus priced options for 13 annual production lots totaling 179 aircraft.

title: The Boeing Company FY2022 Form 10-K — NASA as direct customer: Commercial Crew / CST-100 Starliner (p.88)
key_points: NASA contracted Boeing to design and build the CST-100 Starliner spacecraft to transport crews to the International Space Station.
Boeing successfully completed the uncrewed Orbital Flight Test in Q2 2022; a crewed flight test was expected to be completed in 2023.

During 2022 Boeing increased the Commercial Crew reach-forward loss by $288 (millions), reflecting increased estimated costs to complete crewed flight tests and revised schedules for the crewed flight test and three post-certification missions.
